title: After 52 Years, Salman Khan Is Finally Leaving Galaxy Apartments — and Bollywood's Most Famous Balcony Goes Dark
excerpt: The Khan family has received approval to build a six-storey sea-facing fortress in Bandra. The reason isn't an upgrade — it's survival.
body:
There is a balcony in Bandra that every Indian alive can picture with their eyes closed. First floor, Galaxy Apartments, Band Stand. Salman Khan standing there in a black T-shirt, arms raised, while ten thousand people below scream his name on Eid. That balcony was Bollywood's most public address — more recognizable than any film set, more iconic than any red carpet. Fans pressed against the barricades, phones thrust upward, children on their fathers' shoulders. Year after year, decade after decade.

The balcony has been sealed shut since 2024.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=zwMo9xQ9eAM

And now, the Khan family is preparing to leave Galaxy Apartments altogether.

A New Fortress Rising in Chimbai

On June 16, the Maharashtra Coastal Zone Management Authority (MCZMA) approved the construction of a six-storey sea-facing residential building in Bandra's Chimbai area — just a few hundred metres from Galaxy Apartments. The plot is registered in the name of Salma Khan, Salman's mother. The family purchased it back in 2011. A two-storey house that stood on the property, dating back to before 1956, was demolished after being declared structurally unsafe.

The approved plans include a ground floor, stilt parking, and six upper floors with a total built-up area of approximately 1,040 square metres. It will be developed under Regulation 33(16) of Mumbai's Development Control Regulations by Sach Developers, with an FSI of 1.459. The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) granted the preliminary Intimation of Disapproval approval in October 2025.

No existing trees on the site will be felled. Indigenous species will be planted around the property.

The details sound clinical. The reason behind them is anything but.

The Night That Changed Everything

On April 14, 2024, two bike-borne men fired five rounds outside Galaxy Apartments in the early hours of the morning. The Lawrence Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility. The incident sent shockwaves through the industry and forced an immediate security overhaul. Salman Khan was placed under Y-plus security cover, one of the highest protection categories in India.

The balcony was sealed. The Eid appearances stopped. The man who once walked through Bandra like he owned it — because in a way, he did — became someone who needed armed escorts to leave his own home.

Mumbai Police filed a 1,735-page charge sheet against six arrested accused and three wanted persons, including Lawrence Bishnoi himself. The evidence included statements from 46 witnesses, confessional statements under the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act, and 22 panchanamas.

The investigation confirmed what everyone already sensed: this was not a random act. It was organised, funded, and directed from behind bars.

52 Years at One Address

The Khan family has lived at Galaxy Apartments since 1974. Veteran screenwriter Salim Khan — the man who co-wrote *Sholay*, *Deewaar*, and *Don* — raised all five of his children on the first floor of that building. Salman, Arbaaz, Sohail, Alvira, and Arpita grew up there. Over the decades, most of the siblings moved out. Salman stayed.

For NRIs, Galaxy Apartments was a pilgrimage site. Visiting Mumbai meant standing outside that building, hoping for a glimpse, recording a shaky video of the lit-up windows. The address was as much a part of Salman Khan's identity as his films — the neighbourhood knew him, the chai wallahs knew him, the autorickshaw drivers gave directions to "Salman bhai ka ghar" without blinking.

Leaving is not an aesthetic choice. It is a security imperative.

What the New Home Signals

The new property sits on a quieter lane, away from the main road, in a location expected to offer the family greater privacy and far more robust security infrastructure. Unlike the exposed, street-facing balcony of Galaxy, the new bungalow can be designed from the ground up with modern surveillance, controlled access points, and the kind of perimeter security that a 1970s apartment building was never built to provide.

No official statement has come from the Khan family confirming the move. But the approvals are in place, the land has been owned for 15 years, and the old structure has already been demolished.

Salman Khan is not slowing down professionally. His next theatrical release, the action film Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace, directed by Apoorva Lakhia, is targeting an August 14, 2026 release. He is also shooting SVC63, directed by Vamshi Paidipally and produced by Dil Raju, scheduled for Eid 2027.

But the superstar who once threw open his balcony to the world will soon live behind walls designed to keep that world at a safe distance. Galaxy Apartments will remain standing. The Khan name will remain on the intercom. But the era it represented — a time when Bollywood's biggest star could live on a public street, behind glass doors, one floor up from the pavement — is gone.

The balcony stays sealed. And now, the apartment stays empty.
image_caption: Salman Khan, who is leaving Galaxy Apartments after 52 years following security threats from the Lawrence Bishnoi gang (Wikimedia Commons)
author: Diaspora Desk
